title: Bounded complexes of finite Tor amplitude are perfect
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $K^\bullet$ be a bounded cochain complex of finitely generated $R$-modules [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], and regard it as an object of $D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Fix integers $a\leq b$. Assume that $K^\bullet$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$, meaning that
$$H^i(K^\bullet\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}M)=0$$
for every $R$-module $M$ placed in degree zero and every $i\notin[a,b]$. Here the derived tensor is computed on K-flat module complexes as in [lem-pc-source-kflat-module-tensor-model]. Then there is a complex $E^\bullet$ of finitely generated projective $R$-modules [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], with $E^i=0$ for $i\notin[a,b]$, whose image in $D(R)$ is isomorphic to $K^\bullet$. Thus $K^\bullet$ is perfect over $R$ [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. If $R$ is local, meaning that it has a unique maximal ideal, the model $E^\bullet$ can be chosen finite free [def-weil-pbc-free-module] in the same degrees.

proof.text: For every $i$, the cycles $Z^i=\ker(d_K^i)$ form a submodule of the finite module $K^i$, hence are finitely generated by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite]. Their quotient $H^i(K)=Z^i/\operatorname{im}(d_K^{i-1})$ is generated by the images of any finite generating set of $Z^i$. Boundedness of $K$ gives an upper cohomological bound. The criterion [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-pseudocoherent-cohomology-criterion] therefore makes $K$ pseudo-coherent.

By [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex], choose a bounded-above finite free representative $F^\bullet$ of $K$. Each term is flat by [lem-sc-affine-standard-cover-finite-free-local-fp-flat], so [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat] makes $F$ K-flat: tensoring any acyclic module complex with $F$ is acyclic, exactly the ordinary-module condition [def-pc-module-kflat-complex] required below. Apply [lem-pc-source-kflat-module-tensor-model] with second factor $R[0]$. The ordinary tensor complex $F\otimes_RR$ is isomorphic to $F$ by $x\otimes r\mapsto rx$, with inverse $x\mapsto x\otimes1$; these formulas commute with the differentials. The hypothesis with $M=R$ consequently gives $H^i(K)=0$ outside $[a,b]$, in particular above $b$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-pseudo-coherent-bounded-finite-free-model] to this pseudo-coherent object and the upper bound $b$. It gives a finite free complex $P^\bullet$ with $P^i=0$ for $i>b$ and a quasi-isomorphism $P\to K$. Its terms are flat by [lem-sc-affine-standard-cover-finite-free-local-fp-flat], and it is K-flat by [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat], in the ordinary-module sense [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]. For every $R$-module $M$, [lem-pc-source-kflat-module-tensor-model] identifies the cohomology of the ordinary tensor complex $P\otimes_R M$ with that of $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}M$. Thus $H^{a-1}(P\otimes_R M)=0$ for every $M$, since $a-1<a$.

proof.text: Put $Q=\operatorname{coker}(d_P^{a-1}:P^{a-1}\to P^a)$. The termwise flatness of $P$ and the universal exactness in degree $a-1$ established in step 3 are precisely the hypotheses of [lem-pc-module-flat-opcycles-tor-criterion], so $Q$ is flat. Choose finite bases of $P^{a-1}$ and $P^a$. They express its defining cokernel sequence as $R^{\oplus m}\to R^{\oplus n}\to Q\to0$, so $Q$ is finitely presented (and generated by the images of the $n$ basis vectors). By [lem-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-flat-module-projective], $Q$ is finite projective.

Define $E^i=0$ for $i<a$, $E^a=Q$, and $E^i=P^i$ for $i>a$. Its differential in degree $a$ is induced by $d_P^a$, which annihilates $\operatorname{im}(d_P^{a-1})$ because $d_P^ad_P^{a-1}=0$; above degree $a$ keep the differentials of $P$. These give a complex and a quotient chain map $P\to E$. At degree $a$ its cohomology is $\ker(d_P^a)/\operatorname{im}(d_P^{a-1})$; in degree $a+1$ the image of the incoming differential is unchanged, since $P^a\to Q$ is surjective; all higher cohomology is unchanged. Below $a$ both cohomologies vanish, for $P$ by step 2 and its quasi-isomorphism with $K$, and for $E$ because its terms are zero. Thus $P\to E$ is a quasi-isomorphism by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Its image is invertible in $D(R)$, and $E\cong P\cong K$ in $D(R)$. Since $a\leq b$, $E$ is zero outside $[a,b]$. The bottom term is finite projective by step 4; every other nonzero term is finite free and hence projective by [lem-weil-pbc-free-module-projective]. This is the required model.

source.place: Tag 0658 (more-algebra-lemma-perfect), E = tau_{>= a}F; explicit quotient-truncation cohomology check

proof.text: If $R$ is local, $Q$ is a finitely generated flat module by step 4, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-flat-local-free] makes it free. It has a finite basis: under any free-basis description, the union of the finite supports of a finite generating set is finite and contains every basis vector (over a nonzero ring); the zero module has the empty basis. All terms $E^i$ for $i>a$ already have finite free bases, and the zero terms have the empty basis. Hence the very same model is finite free and remains supported in $[a,b]$.
